Appendix: Recommended Skill Specification Fields When these catalog entries are converted into executable skills, use a consistent specification so they can be evaluated, repaired, reused, and combined safely. Field Definition Purpose The exact user or system outcome the skill is responsible for. Triggers Requests, files, conditions, or workflow states that should activate the skill. Inputs Required and optional data, formats, versions, locales, platforms, and constraints. Outputs Artifacts, reports, structured findings, fixes, evidence, and status returned. Supported Standards Applicable WCAG criteria, platform guidance, document standards, or localization rules. Toolchain Approved scanners, assistive technologies, browsers, devices, parsers, and review environments. Execution Procedure Ordered steps with checkpoints and deterministic handoffs. Pass and Fail Criteria Observable conditions that determine success, failure, severity, and release blocking. Human Review Points Decisions requiring disabled users, translators, linguists, subject experts, or legal owners. Edge Cases Dynamic states, unusual inputs, mixed scripts, offline use, slow networks, errors, and assistive- technology combinations. Evidence Screenshots, transcripts, logs, test cases, sample files, issue references, and verification results. Repair Strategy How to isolate root causes, preserve passing work, implement the smallest fix, and retest regressions. Privacy and Security Rules for recordings, personal data, user-generated content, third parties, and secure retention. Versioning Skill version, standards baseline, dependencies, supported products, and deprecation policy.
